citation.title: An AI-Assisted Design Method for Topology Optimization Without Pre-Optimized Training Data
citation.authors: Alex Halle; L. Flavio Campanile; Alexander Hasse

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: Across 100 random validation cases, the trained network produces a topology in about 8.4 ms versus 1.9 s for the 88-line SIMP optimizer, an approximately 225-fold per-design speedup.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Section 3.2 states roughly 225 times; printed mean times in Figure 14 paragraph are 1.9 s and 8.4 ms (ratio about 226 [derived]).
claim.alternatives: Abstract claims much lower compute effort qualitatively. Section 3.3, Table 5 gives a 5,612-use break-even point after training.

baseline.classical_method: SIMP using Andreassen et al. top88 code with density filter (Sections 3.1-3.2)
baseline.hardware_classical: not stated separately; Table 1 lists the study hardware only
baseline.hardware_ml: Nvidia Titan RTX 24 GB, AMD Ryzen Threadripper 2950X 16-Core, 128 GB RAM, Windows 10 (Section 3.1, Table 1)
baseline.classical_iterations: not stated; baseline uses top88 parameters in Section 3.1, Table 2
baseline.classical_time: 1.9 s mean over 100 validation cases (Section 3.2, Figure 14; Table 5)
baseline.ml_time: 8.4 ms mean per prediction over 100 validation cases (Section 3.2, Figure 14; Table 5)
baseline.data_generation_cost: No pre-optimized training set; random inputs and evaluated candidate geometries generated during training, included in the 2:56:32 training run (Sections 2, 3.2)
baseline.quality_metric: FE-based compliance scatter against top88 (Figure 14b); MSE, MAE and element-density agreement (Table 4); filling and force evaluator losses for examples (Table 3)
baseline.quality_gap: Table 4: mean density MSE 0.093, MAE 0.114, and 79.7% of elements within 0.01 of top88 density; Figure 14b shows compliance scatter, but no matched-quality criterion.

R1.evidence: Section 3.2, Figure 14: inference time is compared with a full top88 run; compliance is shown as a scatter with deviations but no quality-matched speed comparison or stated error bound.

R2.evidence: Sections 1.3 and 3.2: comparator is the 88-line educational top88 MATLAB implementation; neither its sparse solver details nor hardware assignment are stated, so a threshold R2(a)-(e) is not established.

R3.evidence: Sections 2 and 3.2-3.3: candidate generation and evaluation occur within the measured training run of 2:56:32; Table 5 reports a 5,612-prediction break-even including training.

R4.evidence: Section 3.2, Figure 14b evaluates returned designs by compliance and Table 3 gives sample filling losses, but the rate of disconnected, infeasible or failed designs is not reported.

notes: The paper provides validation data at DOI 10.17632/459f33wxf6.2 (Conclusion) and an online demonstration, but no public implementation link. Table 4 reports standard deviations of density agreement measures, not repeated-run timing variance.
